drivingQuestion: Why can a sharecropper who consumed all the produce not establish presumption?
outcomeNote: R' Yoḥanan's setting answers the difficulty

segments.he: אָרִיס אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה. אַמַּאי? עַד הָאִידָּנָא פַּלְגָא, וְהַשְׁתָּא כּוּלַּהּ! אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּאֲרִיסֵי בָּתֵּי אָבוֹת.
segments.en: § The Gemara discusses a ruling that it paraphrases from the mishna: «A sharecropper does not have» the ability to establish the «presumption» of ownership of property in his possession. «Why» not? Isn’t it so that «until that time,» while he was definitely working as a sharecropper, he consumed only «half» of the produce of the land, «and now,» for the past three years, he consumed «all of» its produce? He should be able to establish the presumption of ownership by consuming more produce than a sharecropper does. «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» The ruling of the mishna is stated «with regard to family sharecroppers.» This type of sharecropper, who works for a family for many years, gathers all of the produce into his property, and then returns the landowner’s share. Therefore, his collecting all of the produce into his property does not establish the presumption of ownership.
